Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
246 PM EDT Fri Sep 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 245 PM EDT Friday...

Trending drier for this weekend.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 245 PM EDT Friday...

1. The nor'easter attempts to gain entry into the region this 
weekend and for the start of next week, but the strongest impacts 
will remain over southern New England.

2. Dry and Seasonably Warm next week

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 245 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure will remain centered over Quebec heading 
through tomorrow, keeping the weather mostly dry. Increasing low-
level flow will help keep the boundary layer a bit coupled tonight 
and prevent much fog or frost formation. A few showers are possible 
over southern Vermont late tomorrow, while central and northern 
areas will remain dry with only some high clouds. The nor'easter 
will remain centered off the Mid-Atlantic Coast heading through 
Saturday night and Sunday. Its stationary position will help 
moisture wrap around to the west, and multiple bands of rain 
will move across southern Vermont and attempt to make their way 
north. However, they will be displaced far from the center of 
the low and will be heading into very dry air so by the time 
they reach northern areas, they will mostly fall apart. 
Therefore, while southern Vermont will see multiple rounds of 
showers, northern areas will only see a few sprinkles and mostly
dry weather. As the system occludes and a trough pushes in 
closer from the northwest on Monday and Tuesday, the nor'easter 
will reenter the background flow and get pulled northeast and 
out of the region. As it moves north, multiple rounds of showers
are possible even in northern areas Monday into Monday night. 

Some gusty winds will occur late Saturday into Sunday as the low-
level jet moves overhead, particularly in southern Vermont. It 
should have winds in the 35-50 KT at around summit level, and 30-40 
KT looks to be under the inversion level. This will likely cause 
increased gusts along the western slopes due to downsloping, but 
even if conditions become very favorable, the strength of the low-
level jet will limit gusts. Therefore, gusts in the 30-40 mph range 
are possible along the western slopes of the southern Greens.

KEY MESSAGE 2: High pressure moves in Tuesday as our nor'easter moves 
out to sea. We'll have a warming trend through Thursday, with 
temperatures reaching into the mid-70s in the Champlain Valley. A 
cold front will come through later in the day Thursday bringing some 
rain and dropping our temperatures back into the 60s for most 
locations.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 18Z Saturday...VFR conditions with winds less than 10kt will
continue through the afternoon hours today. Tonight, high clouds
associated with the coastal nor'easter will roll in. These clouds
will prevent radiational fog formation overnight, with the possible
exception of KMSS which will be far enough that the clouds won't
reach until later in the overnight hours. There are also some hints
of a low cloud forming over Lake Champlain and moving over BTV.

Outlook...

Saturday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

Monday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&
